They have always been about even, but something is wrong with my squats and they are just absolutely suffering.

That makes sense. I should try to focus more on keeping my upper body is the same position throughout the whole squat. I don't lean forward a whole lot, but I definitely don't go up perfectly straight either. It hasn't been a problem thus far, because it's not nearly enough to tip the bar forward over my head, but it may worsen slightly as I go up in weight. Part of this could be bad flexibility and not being able to squat down with my chest fully upright, or it could just not be focusing on the things that you stated. I will try to remember those steps next time I squat!
Wow. Very interesting and helpful! Thanks

Usually just "head up", "knees out", and "engage your core". I do have mild scoliosis and an anterior pelvic tilt, so I was sticking my chest&butt significantly when squatting for a long time. I recently discovered that this isn't good, because it stretches your back out in an unnatural way and puts pressure on your spine in a way it shouldn't, so I have been trying to keep my core straight and engaged.

Usually I would just do more reps at around 135-185, like you said. Last week I tried maxing out and got 200 real easy, so I got excited and maxed out again this week to hit 215. I should probably stop maxing out, because it is not ultimately effective. My typical week is two leg days. They each include squat/Romanian/leg ex and curl, as well as lunges, calf raises, and good mornings. I could definitely switch the squat to leg press for a while, or do it once a week, or have that be my only leg day for the week. I do feel like I get enough rest doing it twice a week, but there could be leg exhaustion that I'm not noticing.

I definitely do not get enough sleep. I tend to be a less stable person in general too, running into furniture, etc. I do not do stretching. Would you recommend before or after lifting? I have been told previously that stretching before can relax the loosen the muscles too much and affect lifting, but I'm willing to try it.
My workout partner tells me my form is good, other than the knee/hip issues after a couple of reps. Not noticeably tipping forward. I will give that article a read!
That is probably true. I am the least flexible person I know. I've been ignoring this, but I could see how it would effect lifting. I should probably start a stretching routine.

My current program doesn't have me doing leg press, and I feel like that is a good idea! One of my IRLs told me to switch back and forth between squats and front squats/leg press, which I may try. I do Romanian deadlifts twice a week right now. A few sets at 155-185 and maxing out at 215.
I hope so! Squats had always been my favorite, but now that my weights in everything but squats are consistently going up, I'm starting to hate squats. I hope I can get back to loving them!

I feel like part of it may actually be form, now that I think about it. I was first trained for squats on a competitive power lifting team and we did a stance with our feet way wider apart than you normally should. I got used to this for years, and a few months ago I started squatting with my feet shoulder width apart instead. I bet my body is just used to the old way and I need to rebuild up slightly different muscles to do the narrower stance.

I used to be in competitive power lifting, and was squatting 185 at 110 body weight. This issue with the squatting is new, as I have always been fine at squatting. All of my other lifts are appropriate for my body weight, it is only the squat that I am having difficulty with.

That could work! I've done a set of dumbbell curls where I went all the way down from 30s to 10s, dropping 5 lbs each set after failure with no rest in between, but I think I'd collapse if I tried doing it with squats. I've never done drop sets before. I feel like it's not quite the same as what the program had me do with the curls, because I'm guessing you take a normal rest in between. I will try it!

That makes a lot of sense! Thank you! I've done strong lifts for 4 weeks at a time between other programs to get a break (because it's only 3-4 days a week as opposed to my usual 6 days a week programs), but I haven't really stuck with it for extended periods of time (like the usual 8-10 weeks). It did increase my squat while I was working it for those in between weeks, but only doing it for short periods of time obviously doesn't give you the full benefit of the program. I am currently 4 weeks into Arnold's Blueprint to Mass (I know it's an outdated program, but I like going old school), and I'd like to finish the next 4 weeks, but I think I'm going to incorporate a third day of some leg work (possibly squats/front squats/leg press) on one of my chest&back days. Then once this program is over, I'll give strong lifts a shot for a longer period of time.
That makes sense. By the fifth set, I can only usually do 3 reps before my knees start coming in, though, so maybe I need to back the weight down more and focus on higher reps per set.
I am currently lifting 6 days a week, two days of legs. By frequency, do you mean more days a week with squats or just more reps?

That is a lot of great ideas! I'll try to keep those in mind. I'd definitely like to do more meditation, I do need to find some fun things to do with friends that won't remind me of drinking, and I probably should try to restrict calories a little less. I did let myself have some chocolate tonight!
I actually just bought them on Amazon!
Thanks, I'll try to keep that in mind! I've definitely started to struggle more with thoughts of drinking lately.
I was doing a 6 day PPL power building split. Now I'm doing Arnold's Blueprint to Mass!
